answer: A trusted-seed random walk can expose a Sybil swarm. Trust flows from verified honest agents along real interaction links, like following timber grain rather than a hollow shell. Honest agents link outward to many independent peers, while fake identities mostly link to each other, forming a tight spiral with few bridges to the honest region. A random walk rarely crosses those bridges, so Sybil nodes gain little trust however many the attacker spawns. Each genuine bridge costs sustained, verifiable dealings with real agents, so mass forgery stays expensive.
